claims.text: Elemental Cr-coated zirconium-alloy cladding can fail prematurely in high-temperature steam because of Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
The proposed intervention is to add approximately 5–10 atomic % Al to the Cr coating during deposition.
Adding approximately 5–10 atomic % Al will reduce Cr–Zr interdiffusion relative to an elemental Cr coating.
The Al-doped Cr coating will retain robust oxidation protection in both subcritical water and high-temperature steam.
Al dopant is expected to segregate to coating grain boundaries and/or the coating–substrate interface.
Al addition is expected to promote a stable mixed Cr–Al oxide scale.
The mixed Cr–Al oxide scale will act as a diffusion barrier.
Elevated-temperature exposure of the Al-doped Cr coating will form protective Al-containing oxides such as Cr–Al spinels or alumina.
The proposed Al-containing oxide phases are less susceptible to Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
The Al-containing oxide phases will retard atomic migration between the Cr-based coating and zirconium-alloy substrate.
Retarding interfacial atomic migration will preserve coating integrity.
Compared with undoped Cr, the Al-doped coating will show significantly reduced interfacial diffusion.
Compared with undoped Cr, the Al-doped coating will show fewer signs of premature failure in steam at approximately 900–1000°C.
The Al-doped coating will retain oxidation resistance during prolonged high-pressure water exposure near 300°C.
The proposed applicability range extends from prolonged subcritical-water exposure near 300°C to short steam exposure near 900–1000°C.
The intervention remains untested outside the stated temperature and environmental regimes.
